findings.problem: The same argument is written out five times in the file, plus the general local version `hIprod` in `solution`. To show that `p * conj q` is integrable on 𝓕, each copy applies `integrableOn_of_bdd` with the continuity of `p.mul (continuous_conj.comp q)`. It then rewrites with `norm_mul, Complex.norm_conj` and closes with `mul_le_mul` plus a `norm_nonneg` side goal. The copies are hi1 and hi2 (lines 331–340), hI and hJ in key_L2 (lines 409–416), and hIprod in `solution` (lines 635–644). hIprod is the general form, but it is local to `solution`. The other proofs repeat the argument by hand with ad hoc projections like `(hB g hg).2.2.2.1 d`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a top-level lemma in PartB right after `integrableOn_of_bdd` (line 311), with the same hypotheses h𝓕m, h𝓕s and hfin:

theorem integrableOn_mul_conj_of_bdd {e₁ e₂ : ℝ} (𝓕) (h𝓕m) (h𝓕s) (hfin) {p q : AdelicGL2 (𝓞 K) K → ℂ} (hp : Continuous p) (hq : Continuous q) {Cp Cq : ℝ} (hCp : ∀ g, ideleNorm K (det g) ∈ Set.Icc e₁ e₂ → ‖p g‖ ≤ Cp) (hCq : ∀ g, ideleNorm K (det g) ∈ Set.Icc e₁ e₂ → ‖q g‖ ≤ Cq) : IntegrableOn (fun g => p g * conj (q g)) 𝓕 (μK).

The proof is the body of hIprod: apply `integrableOn_of_bdd` with `C := Cp * Cq`, then `rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_conj]`, then `mul_le_mul`.

The call sites then become:
- hi1 := integrableOn_mul_conj_of_bdd 𝓕 h𝓕m h𝓕s hfin hDy hxc (fun g hg => (hB g hg).2.2.1) (fun g hg => (hB g hg).2.1)
- hi2 := the same with hyc, hDx, (hB g hg).1 and (hB g hg).2.2.2
- hI d and hJ d: the same pattern with the projections from key_L2's hB
- the iF…jV2 lines in `solution`: replace `hIprod …` with the lemma, and delete the local hIprod (lines 635–644).
findings.benefit: This removes five repeated blocks (about 25 lines) and the local `hIprod`. Each integrability fact becomes a one-line call whose bound hypotheses are visible. The `norm_conj` and `mul_le_mul` argument is maintained in one place instead of six.

findings.problem: `partA` (lines 253–267) and `solution` (lines 579–594) open with the same script. Both pick g₀ with x g₀ ≠ 0 and take the slab from `slab_around`. Both build the fundamental domain 𝓕 on that slab and prove finite volume with `rwa [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr h𝓕s] at h`. Both then destructure `cut_packageC`, extract hxs, the continuity of the first and second derivatives from `hxS [d]` and `hxS [d, d']`, and call `u1_bounds`. The finite-volume derivation (intersecting the slab with 𝓕 via `Set.inter_eq_left`) is the non-routine part. Any change to the cut or slab hypotheses has to be made twice, with the variables renamed (hxD/hxDD against hDc/hDDc).
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma in U6C, for example `slab_setup`. Its hypotheses are those of `cut_packageC`, plus `x ≠ 0`. Its conclusion is ∃ g₀ e₁ e₂ 𝓕, 0 < e₁ ∧ e₁ < e₂ ∧ ideleNorm (det g₀) ∈ Set.Ioo e₁ e₂ ∧ x g₀ ≠ 0 ∧ MeasurableSet 𝓕 ∧ 𝓕 ⊆ {slab} ∧ IsFundamentalDomain … 𝓕 (…) ∧ μ 𝓕 < ⊤.

The proof is the lines 253–261 body: `slab_around`, the existence theorem, and the finite-volume rewrite. A second small lemma can state `hxs`, `hxD` and `hxDD` from `hxS`: for any x with ∀ l, IsArchSmoothAtComplex hw (l.foldr …) ∧ Continuous (l.foldr …), the three facts hold. The statement of the second lemma is `IsArchSmoothAtComplex hw x ∧ (∀ d, Continuous (Dc d x)) ∧ (∀ d d', Continuous (Dc d (Dc d' x)))`.

Both `partA` and `solution` would then start with `obtain ⟨g₀, e₁, e₂, 𝓕, …⟩ := slab_setup …`.
findings.benefit: This removes about 15 duplicated lines of non-trivial measure-theoretic setup from each of the two long proofs. The slab and fundamental-domain construction is stated once, and the main Casimir arguments are easier to read.
